Definition: from G2204; boiled, i.e. (by implication) calid (figuratively, fervent):--hot.
BiblicalUsage: Hot — boiled, burning — is the word, and it appears only in the letter to Laodicea. ‘I would thou wert cold or hot,’ the Lord says, ‘because thou art lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will spue thee out of my mouth.’ Hot is what He wanted; lukewarm is what He could not bear.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that lukewarm is the most dangerous temperature: cold knows it needs heat, but lukewarm thinks it is fine.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
